text: The broker instruction is declared as the S9 activity Partner.issueInstruction with an additive request element (the instruction type, the partner reference, the asset reference, the listing reference and the fee and term references) and an additive answer element (the instruction reference and the issued-at time); the case-move answer is the stage outcome the parent CaseWorkflow applies, carrying the rule ID and its version; the template price of R-DIS-24 is read from P6 rwb-comms with the template code, its language and its version; the auto-debit request of R-DIS-25 goes to P8 rwb-payment with the case, the rental terms and the mandate reference; the broker fee and the broker terms are additive columns of asset_sale in rwb_asset (the fee, its basis, its currency, the instruction term and the terms reference) created by the DB story of this service under DP-15; every value of the fee, the term and the price stays route data, template data or rule data read with its version.
why: No source gives the instruction properties, the case-move operation, the template read, the auto-debit request, the fee or the term a shape or a value, and TSD S5 T3.1 gives listing and asset_sale no fee or term column, while both stories need one fixed shape to build and to test on Day 1.

text: The four legacy criteria stay word for word on the app story; the rule table carries R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25, R-DIS-26, R-DIS-64 and R-DIS-65 verbatim, with R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25 and R-DIS-26 the rules the criteria test and R-DIS-64 and R-DIS-65 tabled because AC1 tracks the route to the sale; the broker state is BROKER_INSTRUCTED from R-DIS-26; the rental terms and the auto-debit are built by RWB-S5-E4033-APP on the same step and this story answers the move from that outcome; the buy-back terms of R-DIS-24 have no other owner because FEAT-AST-23's criteria test R-DIS-66; and the broker fee and terms have no rule row, so they are read as route data.
why: The legacy feature is titled for the broker route while two of its criteria are the buy-back and rental rules, R-DIS-25 is duplicated in legacy RWB-E4-033, and the broker rule names a state and an instruction but no fee and no term, so the step boundary of the three routes has to be stated rather than assumed.

text: The service owns two published events under the Architecture catalogue, AssetTakenOn and AssetSold, and this step publishes neither: AssetTakenOn belongs to the take-on story and AssetSold to the sale story that records the sale. The baseline declares no event element, no producer role and no outbox row for this step, names TSD S5 T5.3 as the source that lists one event only, and leaves the correction of that list to the sale story and the catalogue owner.
why: R-PREC puts the Architecture v5 catalogue first and it gives two events to the topic, while the module technical specification and the context pack give one, and neither the take-on nor the sale belongs to this step, so the boundary has to be stated rather than inferred from either list.
